comparison.objective: Distinct: commission and lock a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative dynamic tuning, versus placing two glazing blocks and standing a glass unit on them.
comparison.physical_skill: Distinct: recessed hex-key engagement, bimanual counterholding, setscrew loosening/retightening, fine collar rotation, guarded cycling, and response-based adjustment versus block placement and controlled glass lowering into a narrow channel. Generic alignment and bimanual control are shared only at the primitive level.
comparison.success_condition: Distinct: two repeatable ≥0.85 J impact cycles within the damper velocity/stroke envelope, with no bottoming, hard-stop strike, overload, excessive rebound, or lock drift, versus released and stable glass resting on two positioned blocks without ever touching the sill, with specified pose/placement tolerances.
comparison.reason: All six indexed specification versions were read. PR-138 tests sequenced support placement and damage-avoiding insertion of a fragile panel; the candidate tests tool-mediated unlocking, dynamic parameter tuning, relocking, and retention under repeated impacts. PR-138 specifies placement, release, stillness, and no-sill-contact thresholds but does not simulate breakage or contact forces. The candidate leaves numeric thresholds for excessive rebound, overload, and allowable collar drift to be declared and lacks manufacturer collar torque/friction calibration; those rubric details must be fixed before implementation, but they do not plausibly duplicate the unrelated glazing objective.
